page: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 8 vCPUs sourced from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as cryptographic capabilities including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, establishing a 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy configurations. Storage includes a bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD intended for temporary storage and high-throughput scratch space. The server does not include discrete GPU accelerators, focusing hardware resources entirely on CPU execution and memory handling.

Synthetic benchmarks reflect strong single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25 percent. Multithreaded benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU evaluations, indicate standard mid-range scaling across the 8 vCPUs. Memory testing highlights an operational tradeoff: while small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 607.78 GB/sec, uncached 256MB read bandwidth measures 37.68 GB/sec, falling into the lower quartile.

Given the high memory-to-core allocation and attached NVMe SSD storage, Microsoft Azure E8ads_v6 is configured for memory-intensive operational workloads. Typical deployments include in-memory key-value stores like Redis, transactional relational databases requiring rapid local tempdb access, enterprise data processing, and mid-tier backend services.
